## 380800: definition, exact correction, and two stronger routes

The actual original math/9906187v2, Definition 12 and Conjecture 13 (p11), and the actual DAM119(2002)217–225 final, p224, define chi_u(G,k)=0 when G has no unique k-list coloring. The corpus omitted this clause. Without it the minimum need not exist, even on an isolated vertex. Both editions print the conjecture for every graph without a connectivity restriction in this passage.

Even with the source definition, G=K2 disjoint-union K1 refutes the equality characterization. For k>=2, changing the color at the isolated vertex in any purported unique proper coloring gives a second proper coloring, so chi_u(G,k)=0. For k=1, a list assignment forces its coloring and its minimum union palette has size chi(G)=2. Thus chi_u(G)=2=Delta(G)+1, but G is neither complete nor an odd cycle. This is a connectivity/equality-domain correction, zero significant-discovery credit. Strong contrary case: it really negates the printed source's unqualified iff, including the final publication. Exclusion is based on the disconnected domain repair, not smallness, shortness or an authenticated earlier printed exact witness.

I pursued the stronger bound itself through local recoloring. In a unique k-list coloring c, every alternative color a in L(v) must occur at a neighbor of v: otherwise recoloring v to a is a second coloring. Hence k-1<=deg(v) for every vertex. If k=Delta+1, all degrees equal Delta and all neighbors of every v have distinct colors, each appearing in L(v). On any edge uv one may swap c(u),c(v): no other neighbor of u has color c(v) and no other neighbor of v has color c(u), so this is a second proper list coloring. Therefore on a nonempty graph with an edge, uniqueness requires k<=Delta (isolated vertices already prohibit k>=2). This pays a list-size constraint, not a palette-size constraint.

Second route: compress the palette of an existing unique coloring. Form a color-conflict graph by requiring the actual color c(v) to differ from every alternative in L(v). A proper recoloring of this conflict graph preserves each list size, but it need not preserve uniqueness: distinct original colors can merge across vertices and create new proper list colorings. Its color degrees also have no bound Delta because one color may occur on arbitrarily many vertices. The unpaid lemma is a Delta+1 palette compression preserving global uniqueness. Complete multipartite examples in the source show that the simpler max{k+1,chi(G)} palette claim already fails for k>=3. No connected counterexample to the full bound or all-parameter palette theorem was obtained.
